v.why: When the direct input-to-output edge is missing, a skip on edge 4 supplies a needed residual path, giving much larger gains than when edge 3 already carries an op.
Replacing an existing skip shortcut on edge 3 with a conv removes the residual path and hurts, whereas filling an empty edge 3 gives large gains.
In conv-heavy cells the edge-3 shortcut is essential for trainability, so removing it costs much more than in pool- or skip-dominated cells, where removal can even help.
Without edge 3, edge 5 is one of few remaining paths to the output, so deleting it is far more damaging.
Adding a conv to an empty edge 1 adds capacity and a path, while replacing a skip there loses a useful identity path.
Pooling on an empty edge 1 adds a path at little cost, whereas overwriting a conv or skip with pooling removes useful computation.
In pool-dominated cells that lack any conv, adding a 3x3 conv supplies the cell's only learnable feature extraction and gives large gains.
Overwriting a 3x3 conv on edge 4 with a skip removes learnable capacity, which is catastrophic in cells where it is the only conv.
Adding the input-to-output residual where none exists greatly improves optimization, more than swapping an existing op on edge 3 for a skip.
When other edges carry skips instead of convs, the cell lacks learnable operations, so adding a 3x3 conv on edge 0 yields much larger gains.

raw:
Ten hypotheses grounded in the 100 measurements and in how NAS-Bench-201 behaves:

1. **Edge 3 is the key shortcut.** The direct input-to-output path (edge 3) dominates the interactions.
   - Adding a skip on edge 4 helps much more when edge 3 is empty (rows 41–44 versus 45–48).
   - Replacing an existing skip on edge 3 with a conv hurts, while filling an empty edge 3 helps hugely (rows 1–10).
   - Removing a skip on edge 3 hurts conv-heavy cells but helps pool-only and skip-only cells (rows 81–90).
2. **Removing edge 5 is worse when edge 3 is already empty.** The cell is left with fewer paths to the output (rows 11 and 20).
3. **Filling an empty edge beats overwriting an existing op.** Adding a conv to an empty edge 1 beats replacing a skip there (rows 91–95 versus 96–100). The same pattern shows for avg_pool on edge 1 (rows 31–40).
4. **Adding a conv helps more in cells that have none.** It matters most in pool-only or skip-only cells (rows 29, 59, 60).
